Adding driver's license digital version to iPhone feature appears set to expand to the 15th U.S. state soon.

Apple currently lists 14 states supporting this feature, along with Puerto Rico, while backend data shows one more is on the way...

Many of us have long hoped to be able to present digital ID documents such as driver's licenses and passports on iPhone or Apple Watch without needing to carry physical ones.

That future may still be some distance away, but Apple took its first step back in 2021, when it announced plans to let iPhone users add their driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app. So far, 14 states have adopted the feature:

  • Arizona
  • Arkansas
  • California
  • Colorado
  • Georgia
  • Hawaii
  • Illinois
  • Iowa
  • Maryland
  • Montana
  • New Mexico
  • North Dakota
  • Ohio
  • West Virginia

Backend data discovered by MacRumors indicates that Oklahoma is about to be added to the list.

We previously provided a detailed walkthrough on how to add a driver's license or state ID to the Wallet app on iPhone. As noted at the time, please bear in mind that digital IDs cannot fully replace physical documents, so unfortunately we still recommend everyone continue to carry a physical copy.

That said, the digital version can still help protect your privacy at eligible TSA checkpoints, and when you need to prove your age to a merchant. The ID confirms you meet the age requirement without disclosing any personal information such as your date of birth.
